newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES WARY OF IRISH MAVERICKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES WARY OF IRISH MAVERICKS.

text.p: Two Australian survivors from the most famous rearguard action in Wallaby history have warned their team mates to expect an Irish backlash at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.

Tim Horan and Jason Little, back at the scene of the Wallabies' epic 1991 World Cup quarter-final when Ireland came within seconds of beating the eventual champions, both anticipate the toughest encounter of their European tour so far.
Irish supporters are in danger of losing faith after the 40-25 defeat by Western Samoa last week which prompted nine changes. But the visitors are less convinced.
Little and Horan point to Australia's record thrashing by New Zealand in Wellington earlier this year, followed just a week later by a storming win over world champions South Africa.

"We're favourites but they play with a lot of passion and spirit. The surprise factor is always there...we're expecting a very tough game," said Horan, restored to his favourite centre position in a Wallaby side showing six changes, two positional, from the team who beat Scotland 29-19 this month.
Little, picked on the wing in preference to David Campese who has been handed a late place on the replacements' bench, admits the Wallabies are also overdue a top-vel performance.

"Hopefully it's going to happen soon...we're running out of time," said Little. "We've got some great individual players in the backs but we haven't put it together...the criticism we've had has been pretty fair."
A knee injury has forced Little to spend most of his tour on the sidelines and he has mixed feelings about his selection on the wing.
"It's been very strange for the last few days. It's more like playing full-back than centre," he admitted.
"I've only played a handful of games there but you never know, it could suit me."
Horan also supports coach Greg Smith's policy of not selecting players on reputation alone.
"It doesn't matter who you are, it's how you perform. If you don't play well, you can't expect to be picked," said Horan.
Ireland will be led for the first time by hooker Keith Wood who confesses to frequent attacks of nerves before a big match.
His squad have spent an unprecedented amount of time training over the past fortnight but full-back Jim Staples is cautious about predicting instant results.
"I'm not trying to buy us time but judge Ireland in four or five months after the Five Nations. Professionalism is new to us. We've got to learn how to make best use of this time."

Ireland - 15-Jim Staples; 14-James Topping, 13-Jonathan Bell, 12-Mark McCall, 11-Dominic Crotty; 10-Paul Burke, 9-Steve McIvor; 8-Anthony Foley, 7-Denis McBride, 6-David Corkery, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Gabriel Fulcher, 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood (captain), 1-Nick Popplewell.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Jason Little, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Tim Horan, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial, 7-David Wilson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Warwick Waugh, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Dan Crowley.
